title: Kernel identity anchoring & NVTX span enrichment for contextual prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: our current prefill/decode telemetry surfaces kernel-level timings and NVTX ranges but lacks a stable, queryable kernel identity and contextual tags that persist across scheduling transformations (batching, KV cache hits, kernel fusion). This ticket adds a compact kernel identity anchoring scheme and NVTX span enrichment so downstream analytics, scheduling heuristics, and the console can correlate kernel choice with request characteristics and scheduler decisions. Goals: (1) attach a compact, stable kernel_id and canonical kernel_kind to every kernel invocation; (2) enrich NVTX spans with contextual tags (prefill/decode phase, scheduling_hint, upstream_request_id, kv_cache_hit_flag); (3) emit lightweight per-kernel histograms and quantiles for exec_latency_ms suitable for high-cardinality rollups; (4) define protobuf/JSON telemetry schema and back-compat strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Every kernel invocation emitted in traces and metrics includes kernel_id and kernel_kind fields
NVTX span names include phase prefix (PF_ / DC_) and contain contextual tags: scheduling_hint, kv_cache_hit, request_route
New per-kernel histogram metric kernel.exec_latency_ms has consistent buckets across runtimes and is available in the metrics pipeline
Existing dashboards can join traces with metrics using kernel_id without high-cardinality explosion (proof with a benchmark query)
No >5% steady-state tail regression on 95th-percentile latency in a controlled canary run
technical_design: Overview: introduce a kernel identity anchor composed of (model_shard_hash, kernel_signature_hash, compile_variant_id) encoded as a 12-byte base62 string to keep telemetry tags small. kernel_kind is a human-readable enum (ATTN_UNFUSED, ATTN_FUSED, MATMUL_FP16, MATMUL_INT8, SOFTMAX, KV_MERGE). NVTX span enrichment: when creating NVTX ranges, emit an envelope tag block with normalized keys: phase, kernel_id, kernel_kind, scheduling_hint, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, request_route, exec_seq_num. For metrics, instrument a lightweight histogram aggregator in runtime that emits quantiles and bucketed counts for kernel.exec_latency_ms and kernel.exec_gpu_cycles (optional) as timeseries with kernel_id as a label. To avoid cardinality blow-up, we will: (1) sample kernel_id labels at 1% for high-cardinality joins but always emit kernel_kind and phase for 100% metrics; (2) provide a fingerprint->canonical map service in telemetry pipeline to rollup noisy kernel IDs by kernel_kind+compile_variant_id. Telemetry format: JSON lines with fields: timestamp, trace_id, span_id, nvtx_span_name, tags (list of short key=val), kernel_metrics (histogram proto encoded as base64). Back-compat: fall back to existing nvtx naming if enrichment layer disabled; telemetry consumer will detect presence of kernel_id and use enriched join path.
implementation_plan: 1) Design encoding for kernel_id and update kernel registry (runtime catalog)
2) Add kernel_kind enum to kernel metadata and expose in kernel selection path
3) Update NVTX wrapper to attach normalized tag block on span creation
4) Implement lightweight histogram collector in runtime hotpath (C++), careful about allocations
5) Add sampling logic for high-cardinality kernel_id emission and a toggle for full tracing in debug builds
6) Update metrics exporter to include new metrics and confirm pipeline compatibility
7) Instrument canary and run analysis queries to validate rollups and dashboards
testing_plan: Unit tests for kernel_id encoder/decoder and kernel registry consistency
Integration test: simulated prefill/decode sequences asserting NVTX spans contain enriched tags
Load test: 50k requests/s synthetic workload to measure telemetry overhead and confirm <3% QPS regression
Canary: deploy to runtime-1.20 canary fleet for two business days and compare tail latencies and metrics cardinality
Dashboard validation: confirm new kernel.exec_latency_ms populates panels and trace->metric joins return expected results
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Drafted ticket and initial design after sync with serving and telemetry teams (Aisha)
2025-02-24: Implemented prototype kernel_id encoder and added kernel_kind to kernel registry (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123)
2025-02-27: NVTX wrapper updated to accept tag block; added unit tests for tag normalization (branch: nvtx-enrich)
2025-03-02: Benchmarked histogram collector microbenchmark: median overhead 0.35% on sample workload; agreed to 1% sampling for kernel_id labels (notes from perf run attached)
review_feedback: PM (Lena Bishop): prefer human-readable kernel_kind for dashboard labeling; ok to keep sampled kernel_id for trace joins
Security (Ravi Singh): ensure kernel_id encoder doesn't leak filesystem or model path info — agreed to use hashed shard ids only
Infra (Marcos Li): caution on histogram cardinality in metrics ingestion; suggested pre-aggregation and a rollout flag
decisions: Use 12-byte base62 kernel_id to balance entropy and tag size
Emit kernel_kind and phase for 100% of metrics; emit kernel_id at 1% sampling for metric traces
Implement fingerprint-rollup service in telemetry pipeline rather than runtime-side aggregation to minimize runtime cost
risks_mitigation: Risk: cardinality explosion in metrics - Mitigation: sampling + pipeline rollups, default telemetry toggle to off for older tenants
Risk: performance regression - Mitigation: microbenchmarks, C++ allocation-free histogram buffer, toggleable feature flag
Risk: noisy joins due to kernel recompiles - Mitigation: include compile_variant_id in kernel_id and maintain short-lived mapping in telemetry pipeline
next_steps: Merge encoder & registry PR and bump runtime protobuf version
Add canary rollout plan and coordinate with observability team for dashboarding queries
Follow-up ticket to implement telemetry pipeline fingerprint-rollup (PM to file after canary)
